title: CRLR/544/2019 of MUSTAKIM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
CRLR No. 544 of 2019
With
CRMA No. 2837/2019 (Compounding Application)
CRMA No. 2838/2019 (Delay condonation application
in time barred CRLR)
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Pranav Singh, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, A.G.A. for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Mr. Sanjay Kumar, Advocate for
respondent no. 2.
This revision has been preferred with a
delay of 64 days.
After considering the grounds taken in the
delay condonation application and also
considering the fact that since the revision is
accompanied with the compounding application
and the parties have resolved their dispute outside
the court, it would be in the interest of justice that
the delay condonation application may be allowed
and consequently the same is allowed.
Revision itself is taken up for orders on the
compounding application filed by parties under
Section 320 of Cr.P.C.
The revisionist is a convict for commission
of an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act and as a consequence of the
judgment of conviction impugned in the present
revision being judgment dated 16.04.2019, as
rendered by the IV Additional Sessions Judge in
Criminal Appeal No. 79 of 2017 'Mustkim vs.
State', which in turn was affirming the judgment
dated 17.03.2017 as rendered by the Court of
Judicial Magistrate I, Roorkee, in Complaint Case
No. 403 of 2015 'Rajendra vs. Mustakim'. As a
consequence thereto, the revisionist has been
directed to undergo a sentence of one year simple
imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 7,50,000/- has
been imposed out of which Rs. 10,000/- has to be
remitted to the State coffers by the revisionist, i.e.
in the treasury of the District.
This revision has been preferred along with
a compounding application filed by the parties
under the joint signature, which has been duly

verified by the respective counsels for the parties
to the revision. The respondent no. 2 is present in
person duly identified by the counsel, as far as the
revisionist is concerned, since he has been taken
in custody after the judgment of conviction,
presently he is represented through his brother,
who is present before this Court, identified by the
counsel for the revisionist.
Learned counsel for the respondent and the
complainant, who is present in person, has
submitted that in pursuance to the settlement,
which has been arrived at and particularly as
projected in paragraph 3 of the compounding
application preferred under Section 320 of
Cr.P.C., he has admitted the fact that the amount
due and directed to be paid to him to the sum of
Rs. 7,47,000/- to the complainant has already been
remitted by the revisionist and the said fact of
receipt of the said amount is acknowledged by the
complainant/respondent, who is present before
this Court, who had made the statement of having
received the amount.
In view of the aforesaid settlement arrived
at between the parties and in view of the fact that
the total amount due to be paid to the complainant
has been received by him and he has expressed his
intention not to prosecute the complaint any
further, this revision stands allowed.
Even otherwise also, the nature of dispute
for which the conviction order has been passed
against the revisionist is arising out of a private
complaint case and the nature of dispute happens
to be of a private nature and it does not involve
carrying an adverse message to the public at large.
Even otherwise in the situation where the parties
have settled their private complaint by way of a
settlement, it would be absolutely a futile exercise
to call upon the parties to participate in the
prosecution proceedings.
Consequently, the impugned conviction
order would stand quashed. The balance amount
of Rs. 10,000/-, which has been directed to be
remitted to the treasury is being directed to pay
the same before the treasury of the State within a

period of three weeks from the date of receipt of
certified copy of this order.
As soon as the amount is deposited by the
revisionist even before the prescribed period of
this order, he would be released forthwith from
custody.
It is made clear while quashing the
impugned order under challenge, it will not
amount to quash the part of the order by which the
fine has been imposed by the courts below.
Subject to the above observation, the
revision stands allowed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 19.09.2019
Pooja
